name: Shepparton Art Museum
funding: Greater Shepparton City Council gave A$2.57M of A$3.18M revenue (2024-25), with Creative Victoria. Donors include the Fairley Foundation, Carrillo Gantner, the Zurcas family and Bega Cheese.
watch: Opened 2021. SAM Ltd, a non-profit, took over from the council, which leases it the building for A$1 a year.
records_note: Posts annual reports from 2018-19 with audited accounts, a named 2024-25 donor roll and its directors.

name: Artbank
funding: Commonwealth art-leasing programme inside a federal department. Government funding ended in 1992; leasing income pays for operations and acquisitions.
records_note: Publishes yearly reviews for 2024 and 2025, funds itself by leasing art, names no sponsors, and reports accounts through its parent department.

name: Argos
records_note: Lists its seven-person board but posts no annual report or accounts and names only the Flemish Government as funder.

name: Fondation CAB
funding: Founded 2012 by Hubert Bonnet (Forges de Clabecq steel heir, real estate); partners Pictet, BNP Paribas Fortis, De Bethune, Duvel; members pay EUR 500-2,000.
watch: UNVERIFIED: Founder is sole funder; source of wealth not verified. Founder's wealth is steel (family sold Clabecq stake 1974) and property; banks Pictet and BNP Paribas Fortis are partners but not under campaign.
records_note: Names about 70 supporters, undated, with partners as logos; it posts no annual report or accounts and lists no board.

name: Museum Dhondt-Dhaenens
funding: Flemish Government, Sint-Martens-Latem and the National Lottery. Partners include Christie's, Duvel, Puilaetco, Zwartopwit, Colora Gent, Jet Import and the Willame foundation.
watch: Belgian National Lottery money is a parliament-directed subsidy, so it counts as ordinary public funding.
records_note: Posts annual reports for 2019 to 2025 and names its board and partners; the reports checked carry no financial statements.

name: Fondation Zinsou
funding: Private patronage, budget about 1M EUR in 2015. Zinsou family and major patrons, plus BNP Paribas, Institut français, AFD, Masathis and Open Society Foundations (patron lists, undated).
watch: Free entry. Patrons include Kamel Mennour and Hassanein Hiridjee of Axian. The 50-company figure is not published.
records_note: Names its patrons in two circles, undated, but posts no annual reports, accounts or board list.

name: Casa França-Brasil
funding: Rio de Janeiro state cultural centre; restoration backed by Fundação Roberto Marinho (media).
watch: Renamed Casa Brasil on 27 Jun 2025. Petrobras (under active campaign) is the current official sponsor, selected in its Novos Eixos call.
why_flagged: The former Casa França-Brasil now operates as Casa Brasil, with Petrobras as sponsor through its Novos Eixos call (Ícones da Cultura Brasileira line). The rename date is not confirmed.
records_note: Casa França-Brasil's site has no reports, accounts or board, only a sponsor logo bar that names Petrobras and state government bodies.

name: Museu de Arte Moderna da Bahia
watch: The state tendered the museum's restaurant and pier to private operators in 2024.
records_note: A Bahia state museum run through the cultural institute IPAC; its own site refused connection and IPAC's site posts no museum accounts.

name: Museu Lasar Segall
funding: Federal museum under IBRAM. The 2013 to 2015 renovation cost R$2.5M: R$1.5M from the National Culture Fund and R$1M from Petrobras.
records_note: Its site failed a certificate check and did not open; it is a federal museum under IBRAM, whose reports were not opened.

name: Confederation Centre of the Arts
funding: C$20.7M revenue 2023-24 (C$15.1M public grants incl. C$8.6M capital), C$402k sponsorship; Sobey foundations, Cavendish Farms, CN, TD, BMO, RBC, Pepsico, Maritime Electric.
watch: UNVERIFIED: Not researched. Cavendish Farms (J.D. Irving; sister firm Irving Shipbuilding builds navy destroyers) sponsors; Aug 2025 John A. Macdonald fundraising campaign criticised.
records_note: Posts a 2023-24 report with named donors, sponsors, governors and condensed accounts; the full audited statements are stated to be on its website.

name: Dalhousie Art Gallery
funding: University gallery. Footer logos show Dalhousie University, the Canada Council for the Arts and the City of Halifax.
records_note: The gallery posts nothing itself and shows undated footer logos; parent Dalhousie posts annual financial reports from 2014-15 and names its Board of Governors.

name: Art Gallery of Hamilton
funding: C$7.8M revenue, 177,202 visitors (2024); Canada Council, Ontario Arts Council, City of Hamilton, incite Foundation, BMO, TD, RBC, LiUNA, Peller Estates, CHCH.
watch: UNVERIFIED: Sponsor list in the report not screened. Banks (BMO, TD, RBC), union LiUNA, security firm Garda World, winery Peller Estates, Effort Trust on roster; none under campaign.
why_flagged: Name to know: TD Bank pleaded guilty in October 2024 to US money-laundering conspiracy and Bank Secrecy Act failures, paying about $3B. Banks (BMO, TD, RBC), union LiUNA, security firm Garda World, winery Peller Estates, Effort Trust on roster; none under campaign.
records_note: Posts 14 annual reports from 2011 to 2024 with a donor list and a named board, but only a summary of revenue and expenses.
